input.plan:
# Fix CLIENT local play 404s from extra URL slashes

## What the logs show

Flask returns 200 for `POST /play_media`. The video element then requests the file from `http-server` on port 8001, and that request 404s.

From [journal xeu.txt](/home/willow/.cursor/projects/home-willow-workspace-chromecast-controller/uploads/a7ac1704-ab8b-4bc6-a11a-6d6d9c05f4ec/journal%20xeu.txt):

- Covers: `GET //tv_shows/101%20Dalmatians%20The%20Series/....jpg` → 404
- Play: `GET ///tv_shows/101%20Dalmatians%20The%20Series/101%20Dalmatians%20The%20Series%20-%20s1e4.mp4` → 404

The file is on disk at `/media/usb/t7_shield/media/tv_shows/101 Dalmatians The Series/101 Dalmatians The Series - s1e4.mp4`. The correct request is `http://127.0.0.1:8001/tv_shows/...mp4` (one slash after the port).

## Why this config produces those paths

[`app/config.json`](app/config.json) on the client:

- `content_src`: `/media/usb/t7_shield/media` (no trailing slash)
- `content_url`: `http://127.0.0.1:8001/` (trailing slash)

The scanner stores a relative path by string-replacing the directory ([`media_metadata_collector.py`](app/database/media_metadata_collector.py) line 218). With no trailing slash on the directory, `content_src` and `img_src` are stored as `/tv_shows/...` (leading slash). That leading slash is required for filesystem joins such as `content_directory.content_src || content.content_src`. Do not rewrite stored paths.

Play URLs are SQL concatenations that always insert another `/`:

```106:108:app/database/db_queries.py
       content_directory.content_url || '/' || content.content_src AS url,
       content_directory.content_src || content.content_src AS path,
       content_directory.content_url || '/' || content.img_src AS img_url,
```

`http://127.0.0.1:8001/` + `/` + `/tv_shows/...mp4` → `http://127.0.0.1:8001///tv_shows/...mp4`, which is the play 404. [`play_response_from_metadata`](app/routes/shared.py) copies that `url` into `local_play_url`.

Cover URLs that find the file on disk skip slash collapsing:

```390:390:app/database/db_getter.py
                        item["img_url"] = f'{media_directory.get("content_url")}{img_src}'
```

`http://127.0.0.1:8001/` + `/tv_shows/...jpg` → `http://127.0.0.1:8001//tv_shows/...jpg`, which is the cover 404. The fallback `.replace("//", "/")` still leaves a double slash when the input has three.

http-server 14.1.1 does not collapse extra slashes, so both requests 404 and the `<video>` element stays blank.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  config["content_url ends with slash"] --> sql["SQL inserts another slash"]
  scan["content_src starts with slash"] --> sql
  sql --> triple["///tv_shows/...mp4"]
  triple --> http404["http-server 404"]
  http404 --> blank["Player shell, no video"]
```

## Fix

Add one join helper, for example `join_media_url(base, rel)` in [`app/utils/common.py`](app/utils/common.py) (or next to the DB queries if that module is a better home):

`base.rstrip("/") + "/" + rel.lstrip("/")`

Use the same rule in SQL everywhere a media URL is built:

`rtrim(content_directory.content_url, '/') || '/' || ltrim(content.content_src, '/')`

Apply it to:

- [`app/database/db_queries.py`](app/database/db_queries.py) shelf `url` and `img_url` (leave the filesystem `path` expression unchanged)
- [`app/database/db_getter.py`](app/database/db_getter.py) content-by-id `url` (line 236), tag-shelf `img_url` (line 562), query `img_url` (line 873), and the Python cover joins in `_resolve_content_img_urls` / `_stamp_show_posters` (lines 390–434)
- [`app/utils/clone_manifest.py`](app/utils/clone_manifest.py) `_cover_url`
- [`app/utils/backend_handler.py`](app/utils/backend_handler.py) `img_url` assignment
- [`tests/cast_integration_helpers.py`](tests/cast_integration_helpers.py) so integration URL checks match the app

Update [`tests/test_webpage_builder.py`](tests/test_webpage_builder.py) expectations that currently lock in the double-slash play URL (`http://localhost:8000//tv_shows/...` → a single slash).

## Regression check

Add a unit test that inserts a directory row matching this client (`content_url` ending in `/`, `content_src` starting with `/tv_shows/...`) and asserts the play `url` is `http://127.0.0.1:8001/tv_shows/...mp4`. Assert the same for an image join. Run `pytest tests/ -m "not integration" -q`.

No schema change and no rescan. Existing rows start working as soon as queries use the normalized join.

input.overview: Server local play works because http-server’s working directory is the catalog root. On the client those two directories differ, so `/tv_shows/...` 404s even though the MP4 is on disk. Extra slashes are not the difference: http-server 14 collapses them before the file lookup.
input.plan:
# Why server local play works and the client 404s

Both machines run http-server 14.1.1. That version runs `path.normalize` on the request path before `fs.stat`, so `///tv_shows/...mp4` and `/tv_shows/...mp4` look up the same file. The client journal’s `Error (404): "Not found"` is a missing file after that collapse. A root request on the client (`GET //`) was served, so the process is up and `tv_shows` is not at the directory it is serving.

## The variation

Server catalog root and http-server working directory are the same path. Client catalog root is the `media` subdirectory; the client http-server is started on the USB mount above it.

Server ([app/config.json](app/config.json)), and the same values stored in `content_directory`:

- `content_src`: `/media/raid/` (trailing slash)
- `content_url`: `http://192.168.1.175:8000/`
- [system_services/media_drive_as_webpage.service](system_services/media_drive_as_webpage.service) sets `WorkingDirectory` to that same directory
- Scanned rows are `/tv_shows/...`. The browser asks for `/tv_shows/...`. The file is `/media/raid/tv_shows/...`.

Client (the config from the failure, and [setup_client.sh](setup_client.sh)):

- `content_src`: `/media/usb/t7_shield/media` (no trailing slash; one level below the mount)
- `content_url`: `http://127.0.0.1:8001/`
- `setup_client.sh` mounts the disk at `/media/usb/<label>` and writes the http-server unit with `WorkingDirectory` set to that mount, not to a `media` child (`INSTALL_DIR` is `mount_point`, around the `media_drive_${port}.service` sed)
- The scanner strips `content_src`, so play URLs are still `/tv_shows/101 Dalmatians The Series/...mp4`
- http-server then looks for `/media/usb/t7_shield/tv_shows/...`
- The file is `/media/usb/t7_shield/media/tv_shows/...`

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph server [Server]
    raid["http-server cwd /media/raid/"]
    tvS["tv_shows/episode.mp4"]
    raid --> tvS
  end
  subgraph client [Client]
    mount["http-server cwd /media/usb/t7_shield"]
    mediaDir["media/tv_shows/episode.mp4"]
    mount --> mediaDir
  end
  play["Play URL /tv_shows/episode.mp4"] --> tvS
  play --> missing["lookup tv_shows at mount root"]
```

Flask mode (`SERVER` vs `CLIENT`) does not pick a different play URL. [playback.js](app/static/js/playback.js) sets the video `src` to `local_play_url` in both cases. The server database has the same slash shape as the client (`content_url` ending in `/`, `content_src` starting with `/tv_shows`), and local play still works there.

## What this means for the slash join

The single-slash join already in [app/database/db_queries.py](app/database/db_queries.py) makes the URL prettier. It does not add the missing `media/` segment, so client playback stays a 404 until the served directory and `content_src` are the same directory.

Align them on the client, one of these ways:

- Point `content_src` at the directory http-server is already serving (`/media/usb/t7_shield`) and rescan, or
- Point the `media_drive_8001` unit `WorkingDirectory` at `/media/usb/t7_shield/media` so `/tv_shows/...` matches the current catalog. No rescan.

# Client 404 is the http-server working directory

The updated client catalog matches the files. The request that 404s is the same shape the server serves successfully. The remaining difference is which directory `media_drive_8001` is started in.

## What the new client data shows

Config and `content_directory` are now:

- `content_src`: `/media/usb/t7_shield/media/`
- `content_url`: `http://127.0.0.1:8001/`
- episode row: `/tv_shows/A Bunch of Munsch/A Bunch of Munsch - s1e4.mp4`
- file on disk: `/media/usb/t7_shield/media/tv_shows/A Bunch of Munsch/A Bunch of Munsch.jpg`

After the rescan (`added_at` 18:50 UTC), the 13:54 journal is still:

`GET //tv_shows/A%20Bunch%20of%20Munsch/A%20Bunch%20of%20Munsch.jpg` → 404

Server ([app/config.json](app/config.json)) has the same slash shape and local play works:

- `content_src`: `/media/raid/`
- `content_url`: `http://192.168.1.175:8000/`
- rows stored as `/tv_shows/...`
- [system_services/media_drive_as_webpage.service](system_services/media_drive_as_webpage.service) `WorkingDirectory` is that same `/media/raid/` path

## Why `//tv_shows` 404s on the client only

http-server 14.1.1 runs `path.normalize` before `fs.stat`. `//tv_shows/A Bunch of Munsch/....jpg` becomes `/tv_shows/A Bunch of Munsch/....jpg`, then is joined onto the process working directory:

- cwd `/media/usb/t7_shield/media` → `/media/usb/t7_shield/media/tv_shows/...` (the file that `ls` shows)
- cwd `/media/usb/t7_shield` → `/media/usb/t7_shield/tv_shows/...` (not on disk; 404)

[setup_client.sh](setup_client.sh) writes `media_drive_8001.service` with `WorkingDirectory` set to the USB mount (`/media/usb/t7_shield`), not the `media` child. Changing `app/config.json` and rescanning updates only the catalog. It does not change that unit.

Flask `CLIENT` vs `SERVER` does not build a different play URL. [playback.js](app/static/js/playback.js) assigns `local_play_url` in both modes. The server database also stores `content_url` with a trailing slash and `content_src` with a leading `/tv_shows`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  url["GET /tv_shows/show.jpg"]
  url --> norm["http-server collapses extra slashes"]
  norm --> cwd{"WorkingDirectory"}
  cwd -->|"/media/raid on server"| hit["file found"]
  cwd -->|"/media/usb/t7_shield on client"| miss["tv_shows not at mount root"]
```

## Fix on the client

Point `media_drive_8001` at the catalog root. No rescan.

In `/etc/systemd/system/media_drive_8001.service`, set `WorkingDirectory=/media/usb/t7_shield/media`, then `systemctl daemon-reload` and restart `media_drive_8001.service`.

Confirm with `systemctl cat media_drive_8001.service` before editing: `WorkingDirectory` should currently be `/media/usb/t7_shield`. After restart, `GET /tv_shows/A%20Bunch%20of%20Munsch/A%20Bunch%20of%20Munsch.jpg` on port 8001 should return the jpeg.

content.text:
The catalog and the files now match. The 404 is the directory `http-server` was started in.

`content_src` is `/media/usb/t7_shield/media/`, the episode row is `/tv_shows/A Bunch of Munsch/...`, and that jpeg is on disk under `media/tv_shows`. The server uses the same URL shape (`content_url` ending in `/`, paths starting with `/tv_shows`) and local play works because its `http-server` working directory is `/media/raid/`, the same path as `content_src`.

`http-server` 14 collapses `//tv_shows/...jpg` to `/tv_shows/...jpg` before it looks for the file, then joins that onto its working directory:

- If that directory is `/media/usb/t7_shield/media`, the file is found.
- If it is `/media/usb/t7_shield`, it looks for `/media/usb/t7_shield/tv_shows/...`, which is not there.

`setup_client.sh` writes `media_drive_8001.service` with `WorkingDirectory` set to the USB mount, `/media/usb/t7_shield`. Updating `app/config.json` and rescanning does not change that unit.

On the client, check `systemctl cat media_drive_8001.service`. Set `WorkingDirectory=/media/usb/t7_shield/media`, then `systemctl daemon-reload` and restart `media_drive_8001`. No rescan. After that, `GET /tv_shows/A%20Bunch%20of%20Munsch/A%20Bunch%20of%20Munsch.jpg` on port 8001 should return the image.
